en.html:
The night had passed, and the rain had started again. The black-gray clouds seemed to find Kamakura's sky far too comfortable. They had moved out only for the night, and now they were back, settled in with their full weight.

Drops from the rim of my umbrella touched the back of my hand. They were terribly cold.

en.html:
My talk with Muramasa was only a rerun of the question I had put to myself hundreds and thousands of times through the night. I knew. I knew what I had to do.

Appearing without warning in a town, a village, or any other gathering of people, and annihilating it: the Tempest. The Silver Star. The nightmare of modern Yamato. Ending it was my role.

Because only I could.
Because it was the wish my mother had entrusted to me.
Because that one was my sister.

I had to do it, whatever I had to trample to get there.

As I always had. As, for these two years, I had crushed one life after another under my iron boots.

I would go on. Today as well.

Even Ichijou Ayane, waiting at Ennoji—

en.html:
The silent gaze reaching me from the sword-armor moving in hiding nearby was a nuisance. I ignored it all the same and stood up.

My familiar body was absurdly heavy. If I let my guard down, my knees would give out.

It was as if a weight other than body weight hung from somewhere. Somewhere: inside the skull, deep in the heart, or elsewhere.

It was my mind putting on the load. It was making my limbs creak.

The will to fight Ichijou Ayane. That will was heavy.

That girl had declared she would not forgive. Kageaki Minato, and the sins he had committed. She had told me she would not forgive them.

Condemnation.

The I agrees. Yes, exactly. A sin utterly beyond forgiveness.

A sin that must not be forgiven.

Then why... must I resist?

Is it permitted, such a thing as resisting?

No. It cannot be.

If I have not forgotten the lives I stripped with this hand, the blood-flowers I made bloom with these fingers...

then why should I resist judgment?

Should I not accept it?

If I admit that the condemnation is just, should I not give my body to the executioner's blade...?

Yes. That should be the natural course.

Until now, no one to judge me had appeared. I had only been overlooked.

Now one exists. One holding scales and scythe, judge and executioner both, has come.

Then—

付近を潜行する劒冑から送られてくる、無言の視線
が煩わしい。
　それでも黙殺して、立ち上がる。

　慣れ親しむ肉体は、<ruby>矢鱈<rt>やたら</rt></ruby>と重かった。
　気を緩めれば膝が笑い出す程に。

　体重ではない重みが何処かに懸かっているようでも
ある。
　何処か――頭蓋の中か、心臓の奥か、それ以外か。

　<ruby>精神<rt>こころ</rt></ruby>が負荷を掛けている。
　四肢に軋みを上げさせている。

　綾弥一条と戦う。
　その意思が、重い。

　あの少女は許さないと宣言したのだ。
　湊斗景明を――彼が犯してきた罪業を。許さないと
告げたのだ。

　断罪。

　<ruby>被告<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>は、同意する。
　その通り――到底、許されざる罪だ。

　許されてはならない罪だ。

　ならば、どうして……
　俺は抗わねばならないのか。

　抗うなどという真似が、許されるのか。

　否。
　許されない筈だ。

　この手で剥奪した命を、
　この指で咲かせた血華を、

　忘れないのならば……
　どうして、裁きに抗おう。

　受け入れるべきではないのか。

　<ruby>断罪<rt>さばき</rt></ruby>の正当を認めるならば、
　刑吏の刃に身を委ねるべきではないのか……

　そう。
　それが、当然の筈だ。

　今までは俺を裁く者が現れなかっただけだ。
　見逃されてきただけだ。

　今はいる。
　天秤と鎌を持つ、判事にして処刑人たる者が訪れて
いる。

　ならば――

en.html:
The same question, again.

I was not allowed to flee into ease. To admit the sin, submit to the sentence and offer my one life would bring relief—but the time was not yet.

Not until the mission was done did I have the right to do it.

I knew. I knew.

And yet, I thought. Was that not itself an escape from guilt?

Everyone has something they must do. All that live have a mission to fulfill while alive.

But no one can be immortal. Everyone dies with something left behind.

If so, can a mission be called a reason worth avoiding death? It cannot.

Like every dead person in this world, like the people I killed who lost their futures without warning, should I not also die here with regret, thrashing in agony?

Was that not the proper conclusion...?

問答の繰り返し。

　俺に、安逸への逃避は許されない。
　罪を認め、刑に服し、一命を捧げれば楽になれよう
――だが、まだその時ではない。

　使命を果たし終えた後でなくては、俺にはそうする
資格が無い。

　わかっているのだ。
　わかっているのだ。

　しかし――思う。
　それは、罪からの逃避ではないのかと。

　やらねばならぬ事があるのは誰も同じだ。
　生きとし生けるもの全てが、生きて果たすべき使命
を持っている。

　しかし誰もが不死ではいられない。
　誰もが未練を抱えて死んでゆく。

　そう思えば、使命など、死を避けるに値する理由と
言えようか。
　言えまい。

　この世のあらゆる死者のように――俺に殺され不意
に未来を奪われた人々のように、
　俺もまた無念を抱え、ここでもがき苦しんで死んで
ゆくべきではないのか。

　それこそが正しい帰結ではないのか……

en.html:
She did not need to tell me. If I threw away the duty laid on me, what was lost would be more than my one life. The Silver Star would keep on killing. Driving people mad, scattering its ‘eggs’, raising its doubles.

History would record its name as an unprecedented calamity. I must not let that happen.

I would stop it. The damage was already immense, but I would stop it here at least, so that the line of victims would extend no further.

...But. To do that, today I had to fight Ichijou Ayane.

Throw off her rightful condemnation. Defeat her, trample her, and go on. I must.
